item.title: How to visit Innopolis VM
item.description:
How to visit Innopolis VM#

  1. Open your web browser and type Innopolis VM in the address bar.
  2. Then you will be redirected to the SSO Innopolis University login page.
    • If you see the main page immediately, you are already logged in.
    • If you are not logged in, you will be prompted to enter your Innopolis University credentials (username and password). Then click on the Sign in button.
  3. You will be redirected to the main page of the website.

item.title: Password requirements
item.description:
When you create a virtual machine (VM), you set a password for the administrator account. Follow these rules to avoid creation errors.

Rules#

Requirement Value
Minimum length 12 characters
Maximum length 128 characters
Uppercase letters At least 1 (A–Z)
Lowercase letters At least 1 (a–z)
Numbers At least 1 (0–9)
Special characters At least 1 (`!@#$%^&*()_+-=[]{}

Examples#

Password Result Why
MyStrongPass2026! ✅ Accepted Meets all rules
short1A! ❌ Rejected Too short (8 characters, need 12)
alllowercase123! ❌ Rejected No uppercase letter
NoNumbersHere! ❌ Rejected No digit

item.title: Subscriptions
item.description:
How to create a subscription#

  1. From the main page of the website, click on the NEW button in the left bottom corner.
  2. The new menu will open - click MY ACCOUNT.
  3. Click on the ADD SUBSCRIPTION button.
  4. Modal with subscription creation form will open.
  5. Depending on who you are (student, instructor, worker), you will have different options for subscription creation. For example, for students, you can create a subscription for a specific course or general StudentPublic subscription. If you want a specific subscription, you need to contact IT department of Innopolis University.
  6. The details of the concrete subscription type will appear on the right side of the form when you click it.
  7. When you choose the subscription type - click it and then click the tick button on the right bottom corner.
  8. Then you need to wait while the subscription is being created.
  9. Some time your subscription will have the “Syncing” status. Don’t worry, just wait until it will be “Active”.
  10. After a while, your subscription will change its status to “Active”.

Where to find your subscriptions#

  1. From the main page of the website, click on the My Account button in the left bar.
  2. Click on the SUBSCRIPTIONS section.
  3. You can see all your subscriptions.

item.title: Create a virtual machine (VM)
item.description:
How to create a new VM#

  1. At first, you need to have a subscription to the service (see Subscriptions).
  2. From the main page of the website, click on the VIRTUAL MACHINES button in the left bar.
  3. On the Virtual Machines page, click on the right arrow button OR if you have already created some VMs, click on the NEW button in the left bottom corner and then STANDALONE VIRTUAL MACHINE.
  4. In the opened menu, choose one of two creation methods:
    • FROM GALLERY: Detailed configuration with pre-configured templates. Best for specific requirements. (see How to create a new virtual machine from gallery)
    • Quick Start: Fast creation with basic settings. Best for simple VMs. (sese How to create a new virtual machine via QUICK CREATE)

item.title: Glossary
item.description:
This glossary defines the key terms used in the Innopolis virtual machine (VM) documentation.

A#

Administrator account The default user account on a VM. It has full control over the system. On Linux VMs, this is usually the root user. On Windows VMs, it is the Administrator user.

D#

Dashboard The main web page where you manage your virtual machines and subscriptions. You open it after logging in to Innopolis VM.

item.title: Create a virtual machine (VM) from gallery
item.description:
You chose the FROM GALLERY creation method. This option allows you to configure a VM in detail using pre-configured templates.

How to create a new VM from gallery#

  1. Menu with gallery creating will open.
  2. You can choose the different operating system for your VM and see the details.
  3. When you have chosen, click the right arrow button.
  4. Menu with settings of your VM will open.
  5. Now you need to write the name of your VM into NAME field. Name is required.
  6. Write and confirm the new password for your VM.
  7. If you see the red exclamation mark in the PASSWORD field then the condition on the password is not satisfied (see Password requirements).
  8. If you see the red exclamation mark in the CONFIRM field then the password and confirm password are not equal.
  9. ADMINISTRATOR ACCOUNT may be filled by default and can’t be changed. But in some cases you are required to write your own name inside the field.
  10. Also you can write your ssh key into the SSH KEY field or product key into the PRODUCT KEY field. This is not required.
  11. Save your password, administrator account and ssh key or product key, because you will not be able to see them again.
  12. When you have filled all fields, click the right arrow button.
  13. Then you can set your VM network adapter - where your VM be available.
  14. Now you can click the tick button to save your settings and create VM.

item.title: Connect to a virtual machine (VM)
item.description:
How to connect to your VM#

You have three options to connect to your VM:

  • SSH client — Use PuTTY (Windows) or MobaXterm (Windows, Linux, macOS). Requires an SSH key configured during VM creation.
  • Browser — Connect directly from your web browser (see How to connect to your VM from the browser).
  • SSH by IP — Connect using the VM’s IP address with any SSH client (see How to see the IP of the VM).

How to see the IP of the VM#

  1. On your VM dashboard, find the IP address on the right side of the page.
  2. The IP looks like this: 10.13.127.89.
  3. If there is no IP, see the section “How to create a VM with an explicit IP” (will be updated soon).

How to connect to your VM from the browser#

  1. On your VM dashboard, click the CONNECT button at the bottom.
  2. Choose the connection method. To connect from the browser, click WebConsole.
  3. A new browser window will open with your VM console.
  4. Enter your VM login (see What is my VM login) and press Enter.
  5. Enter your VM password and press Enter.
  6. If you see the message Login is incorrect, you entered the wrong login or password. Try again with the correct credentials.
  7. If you successfully connected, you will see a message like Welcome to Ubuntu… or similar, depending on your VM operating system.

item.title: Create a virtual machine (VM) via Quick Create
item.description:
You chose the QUICK CREATE method. This option allows you to quickly create a VM with basic settings.

How to create a new VM via QUICK CREATE#

  1. Menu with quick start creating will open.
  2. Here you need to write the name of your VM into NAME field. Name is required.
  3. Also choose the subscription type - depending on it you can choose different templates (operating systems) for VM.
  4. Then choose the template (operating system) for your VM.
  5. Write and confirm the new password for your VM.
  6. If you see the red exclamation mark in the PASSWORD field then the condition on the password is not satisfied (see Password requirements).
  7. ADMINISTRATOR ACCOUNT may be filled by default and can’t be changed. But in some cases you are required to write your own name inside the field.
  8. Save your password, administrator account and ssh key or product key, because you will not be able to see them again.
  9. If all fields are filled correctly - click the CREATE VM INSTANCE button.
  10. To see the details of creation - click on the DETAILS button.
  11. You can see the progress of creation of your VM here.
  12. On the VMs page you can see your VM. For some time its status will be “Creating”, then it will change to “Running”.

item.title: Details & credentials
item.description:
How to see details of the created virtual machine (VM)#

  1. From the main page of the website, click on the VIRTUAL MACHINES button in the left bar.
  2. Choose the VM you want to see the details of and click on its NAME.
  3. Then you can see the page with your VM.
  4. If you want to see details, click DASHBOARD button.
  5. Then you can see the page with your VM dashboard.

What is my VM login#

  • The VM login is not displayed after creation. The default login is usually root, admin, or administrator.
  • You can see the login of your VM during VM creation.
  • For QUICK START option, you can see the login in the ADMINISTRATOR ACCOUNT section. The login is most likely lower-case instead of upper-case. Or you are required to fulfill it.
  • For FROM GALLERY option, you can see the login in the ADMINISTRATOR ACCOUNT section.

item.title: Troubleshooting
item.description:
Troubleshooting#

This section helps you diagnose and resolve common issues with Innopolis VM. Each problem follows a structured approach: Symptom, Possible causes, Checks, Solutions, and Escalation.

Gray screen — cannot click anything#

Symptom:
The screen turned gray and you cannot interact with the interface.

Possible causes:

  • Your session has timed out due to inactivity.
  • The browser lost connection to the server.
  • The browser tab is unresponsive.

Checks:

  1. Look at the bottom of the screen for a message like «Your session timed out. Click OK to log in again».
  2. Check your internet connection.
